detail.longDescription:
We use the standard Fedora 44 Docker image in our GitLab CI/CD pipeline. At the end, in the after_script section of the pipeline, we collect some metadata to send out via an email. In this data collection, I use the tail command and some awk as I am only interested in a specific section of the last line. However, no matter what I try, the command just doesn't seem to work. Here is the loop in which I collect the data and parse it into a Markdown table format, including debug commands: for file in /tmp/log/logfiles/* ; do printf "File path: $file
" printf "Full file:" cat $file printf "Last line (loose)
" tail -n 1 $file printf "Last line (whole): $(tail -n 1 $file)
" STATUS_LAST_JOB="$(tail -n 1 $file | awk -F ' - ' '{ print $5 }')" printf "STATUS_LAST_JOB: $STATUS_LAST_JOB
" if [[ "$STATUS_LAST_JOB" == "FAILED" ]]; then STATUS_RESULT='failed' elif [[ "$STATUS_LAST_JOB" == "UNREACHABLE" ]]; then STATUS_RESULT='failed' elif [[ "$STATUS_LAST_JOB" == "ASYNC_FAILED" ]]; then STATUS_RESULT='failed' else STATUS_RESULT='succeeded' fi printf "| $(basename $file) | $STATUS_RESULT |
" >> /tmp/issue_description.txt done I have ensured that the tail command is available by specifying dnf install coreutils --assumeyes in the job's before_script section 1 . I verify that it is installed and working by executing which tail and tail --version - both of which succeed and give the expected output: # output /usr/sbin/tail tail (GNU coreutils) 9.10 Copyright (C) 2026 Free Software Foundation, Inc. License GPLv3+: GNU GPL version 3 or later <https://gnu.org/licenses/gpl.html>. This is free software: you are free to change and redistribute it. There is NO WARRANTY, to the extent permitted by law. Written by Paul Rubin, David MacKenzie, Ian Lance Taylor, and Jim Meyering. I have also verified that the container runs in bash. When I tried to ensure running bash with a chsh command, it failed as such: # output /usr/bin/bash: line 266: chsh: command not found While it is an error, it does verify that bash is the shell being used. Now, onto the output of the debugging in the loop itself. Observe the commands and (anonymized) output below: # printf "File path: $file
" File path: /tmp/log/logfiles/logfile5 # printf "Full file:" # cat $file ***log contents*** # printf "Last line (loose)
" # tail -n 1 $file Last line (loose) # printf "Last line (whole): $(tail -n 1 $file)
" Last line (whole): # printf "STATUS_LAST_JOB: $STATUS_LAST_JOB
" STATUS_LAST_JOB: As you can see, I've checked to see if the issue was with my shell formatting and with the files themselves, but it really seems to be the tail command itself. Finally, I should mention that these logfiles are no longer being edited when these commands run, so the -f following utility of tail is not applicable. They are generated by a process in the job's main script, this runs after that has finished. I am at a loss as to why this simple shell utility wouldn't work here. I don't know if it's a GitLab thing, a Fedora thing, a Docker/Podman thing, or something else. What may be going on, and/or what further debugging I can do to troubleshoot? Workarounds are also welcome. 1 I am aware that preparing an actual image with the necessary tools pre-installed is much better. Hopefully we will have the internal container registry up soon so we can do that, but for now, this is unfortunately the only way to accomplish what we want.
